title.english: Khawla bint Iyas ibn Ja'far al-Hanafiyya, the mother of Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.

segments.arabic:
١١١١٤- خولة بنت إياس
بن جعفر الحنفية، والدة محمد بن علي بن أبي طالب.
رآها النبيّ ﷺ في منزله فضحك، ثم قال: «يا عليّ، أما إنّك تتزوّجها من بعدي، وستلد لك غلاما فسمّه باسمي وكنّه بكنيتي وانحله» .
رويناه في فوائد أبي الحسن أحمد بن عثمان الأدمي، من طريق إبراهيم بن عمر بن كيسان، عن أبي جبير عن أبيه قنبر حاجب علي، قال: رآني عليّ ... فذكره، وسنده ضعيف وثبوت صحبتها مع ذلك يتوقّف على أنها كانت حينئذ مسلمة.
segments.english:
11114 — Khawla bint Iyas ibn Ja'far al-Hanafiyya, the mother of Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw her in his house and laughed. He then said: “O 'Ali, you will indeed marry her after me, and she will bear you a boy. Name him with my name, give him my kunyah, and bestow [something] upon him.”

We transmitted it in the Fawa'id of Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn 'Uthman al-Adami, by way of Ibrahim ibn 'Umar ibn Kaysan, from Abu Jubayr, from his father Qanbar, 'Ali's chamberlain, who said: “'Ali saw me ...”—and he related it. Its chain of transmission is weak. Even so, establishing her status as a Companion depends upon her having been a Muslim at that time.

unresolved.explanation: The verb denotes bestowing or granting, but its object is omitted. The Urdu witness omits the entire command, and the collateral evidence does not identify what was to be bestowed. The bracketed “something” preserves the omission without inventing an object.
